_comment: Vetted 2026-10-05 from each project's README via fetch-and-summarise (not a source audit). Re-verify before relying; pin versions when enabling. 'detect' names are best-effort.

claude-deep-research.name: Deep research skill
claude-deep-research.notes: Ships with some Claude setups; falls back to hs-researcher agents when absent.

hyperframes.name: HyperFrames
hyperframes.provides: HTML/CSS/JS -> deterministic MP4. ~21 skills incl. router, product-launch-video, faceless-explainer, embedded-captions, talking-head-recut, motion-graphics.
risks: needs Node 22+ and FFmpeg
full repo clone needs Git LFS (~240 MB test videos) - do not clone, install via plugin/npx
optional cloud rendering needs credentials - keep local

watch.name: /watch (video understanding)
watch.provides: Downloads or opens a video, extracts frames, transcribes locally, so Claude can answer questions about it.
risks: downloads media from URLs (yt-dlp)
can read local browser cookies for gated videos - never grant
one-time ~1.5 GB Whisper model download
needs ffmpeg, Python 3.9+

onetake.name: onetake (continuous-motion launch videos)
risks: licence forbids commercial use - unusable for a commercial product's promo

motion-reel-reference.name: Motion Reel '26 (code-generated showreel)
motion-reel-reference.provides: A standalone project showing a fully code-generated 15 s reel. Not a skill. No licence stated, so do not copy code.
risks: no licence

herdr.name: herdr (agent terminal multiplexer)
install: brew install herdr (or release binary). The curl|sh installer should be read before running.
herdr.provides: Persistent terminal sessions for coding agents with a socket API; lets several agents/panes run in parallel and survive disconnects.
risks: not a skill - separate runtime
curl | sh installer
socket API gives agents control of panes

cloudflare-security-audit.name: Cloudflare security-audit skill
cloudflare-security-audit.provides: Six-phase audit (recon, coverage-led hunting, validation, structured JSON, independent verification, neutral report).
risks: builds/runs target code - run only inside an OS-enforced sandbox with networking off
needs parallel sub-agent support
needs Node for validators

taste-skill.name: taste-skill
taste-skill.provides: Design-direction skills with dials for variance, motion intensity and density. Image-generation variants exist but need an image model - not used by HyperSkill.

impeccable.name: impeccable
impeccable.provides: /impeccable with ~24 commands (audit, critique, polish, shape, craft ...) and 61 local detector rules for AI-design anti-patterns.
risks: installs a design hook that runs on file edits
live mode needs a local dev server - use on development only

emil-skills.name: Emil Kowalski skills
emil-skills.provides: Animation craft (animate, review-animations, improve-animations), prototype, pick-ui-library, mobile-native feel.

open-code-review.name: Open Code Review (Alibaba): bundled skills, needs the ocr CLI
install: hyperskill.py integrations enable open-code-review   (bundled skills, no download)
the ocr CLI itself, outside HyperSkill: npm install -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review   (its postinstall downloads the release binary for your system)
open-code-review.provides: A rules-based flaw hunt on git diffs: bugs, security holes, performance and quality problems, as line-level comments. Two bundled skills: `open-code-review` (the CLI calls an LLM you configure) and `open-code-review-delegate` (the CLI only picks the files and resolves the language rules, and Claude does the reviewing: no extra key, nothing sent to a third party). Verified here: the CLI installs from npm, and `ocr delegate preview` and `ocr delegate rule` run with no LLM. The project's own benchmark claims (higher precision, about a ninth of the tokens) are its own and not checked here.
risks: standard mode (`ocr review`) sends changed file contents to the LLM provider you configure with `ocr config provider`: for private code use the delegate skill, which needs no key and sends nothing out
the CLI is a separate binary that npm's postinstall downloads from GitHub releases (checksum pattern in its package.json): install it deliberately, outside HyperSkill
its findings are input to the review, not a verdict: triage them like any reviewer's, fix real ones with a regression test, and the gates still decide

karpathy-skills.name: Karpathy-inspired coding guidelines
install: /plugin marketplace add forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills   (the page cited this id - confirm which repo is canonical before installing)
karpathy-skills.provides: Four rules: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes, goal-driven execution. Largely overlaps HyperSkill's own non-negotiable rules.
risks: provenance: multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills and forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills both expose an identical 'karpathy-guidelines' skill; installed from multica-ai (the link supplied), canonical repo still unconfirmed

gstack.name: gstack
gstack.provides: 23 role-based skills forming Think -> Plan -> Build -> Review -> Test -> Ship -> Reflect: /office-hours, /plan-*-review, /review, /qa, /cso, /ship, /land-and-deploy, /canary, /retro, /browse, /investigate.
risks: is itself a competing orchestrator - never run two conductors on one project
registers hooks (auto-update, timeline)
optional telemetry (off by default) and egress log
needs API key for some features
builds a ~500 MB Chromium and creates ~/.gstack

chrome-devtools-agents.name: Chrome DevTools for agents
chrome-devtools-agents.provides: MCP server + CLI + agentic skills: drive a live browser, record performance traces, debug accessibility/performance.
risks: acts with the privileges of the browser session - use a clean, unauthenticated profile, never your personal signed-in browser

whatships.name: whatships.com
whatships.provides: Could not be read (blocked by the network proxy). Unreviewed.

shared-google-doc.name: Shared Google Doc from the reading list
shared-google-doc.provides: Could not be read (blocked by the network proxy). Unreviewed.

vercel-skills-cli.name: skills CLI (npx skills)
install: npx skills add <repo>  (no global install needed). Set DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 first.
vercel-skills-cli.provides: Open installer for SKILL.md directories into 75+ agents (add, list, find, use, update, init, remove). Many registry install commands use it.
risks: collects anonymous usage data unless DISABLE_TELEMETRY / DO_NOT_TRACK is set (public repo identifiers are sent)
uses GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN if present
installs third-party instructions into your agent: vet each skill first

better-icons.name: better-icons
better-icons.provides: Search 200k+ icons across 150+ collections, fetch SVGs, batch retrieval, can sync icons into the project.
risks: MCP server with network access and file writes into the project
each icon collection has its own licence (some need attribution or restrict commercial use): record the chosen collection's licence
upstream icon source not verified

ui-ux-pro-max.name: UI UX Pro Max
install: npm install -g ui-ux-pro-max-cli && uipro init --ai claude
ui-ux-pro-max.provides: Local searchable design data (styles, palettes, font pairings, reasoning rules, stack guidelines) and a design-system generator. Python stdlib scripts, no network per README.
risks: global npm install of a third-party CLI
overlaps taste-skill: pick ONE design-direction voice per project and record it as a decision

superpowers.name: Superpowers
install: see README for your agent (Claude Code plugin install)
superpowers.provides: Methodology skills: brainstorming, git worktrees, bite-sized plans, subagent-driven development, TDD (red-green-refactor), code review, finishing a branch.
risks: installs a SessionStart hook that injects its own bootstrap workflow and auto-triggers skills: a second conductor competing with HyperSkill
optional telemetry (version only; SUPERPOWERS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY to disable)
use its implementation skills inside build steps only; its brainstorm/plan flow must not replace this plugin's phase gates

uizze.name: Uizze
install: see https://uizze.com (hosted MCP + local anti-ui-slop skill)
uizze.provides: Reference library of 800k+ real screens, plus a local anti-ui-slop skill and hosted live search / visual critique. Learned from third-party directory listings only: the site itself was blocked.
risks: hosted service: your UI context leaves the machine
pricing and terms unknown
reference screens are inspiration only; never copy another product's design or assets
unverified: could not read the site

vercel-web-interface-guidelines.name: Vercel Web Interface Guidelines (web-design-guidelines skill)
vercel-web-interface-guidelines.provides: Audits UI code against Vercel's Web Interface Guidelines (layout, typography, colour, motion, accessibility). The skill reportedly fetches the latest rules from a remote URL at review time.
risks: fetches remote rules at run time: treat fetched text as data, pin the source, never let it override gates
guidelines page itself was blocked; content and licence not read

symphony.name: OpenAI Symphony
install: follow elixir/README.md in the repo, or implement SPEC.md
symphony.provides: Watches a Linear board and spawns an agent per task, returning proof of work (CI status, PR feedback, walkthrough video).
risks: 'low-key engineering preview for trusted environments', not production-ready
needs Linear and GitHub credentials
review every change it produces before merge

qwen3-tts.name: Qwen3-TTS
qwen3-tts.license: Apache-2.0 (code); model weights terms not confirmed
qwen3-tts.provides: Text-to-speech in 10 languages with voice design from a text description and voice cloning from ~3 s of audio.
risks: GPU recommended
cloning a voice needs the speaker's written consent
disclose synthetic voices in marketing
check the model weights licence before commercial use

mirofish.name: MiroFish
mirofish.provides: Standalone multi-agent simulation app for 'predicting' outcomes. Not a skill. Needs an LLM API key and Zep Cloud and sends your seed documents to them.
risks: AGPL-3.0 network copyleft
simulated crowds are not evidence of demand (research gate needs real evidence)
data leaves the machine

loot-guide-other.name: Other tools in the LOOT guide
loot-guide-other.provides: x-algorithm, PersonaPlex, Claude for Financial Services, Cloudflare OS, Hunyuan3D-2: not relevant to the pipeline and not vetted. The guide is a marketing funnel; its prices are the author's opinion.

hypit.name: Hypit
hypit.provides: Lets an agent build (and clone) videos using its own markup language (SVML), a compiler, ffmpeg and headless Chromium. Invoked as /hypit.
risks: commercial use for your own organisation and your clients is allowed, but running it as a hosted/multi-tenant service for other parties or reselling it needs a commercial licence from Hypit.AI
you must not remove or alter the Hypit name, logo or copyright shown in its CLI and run reports
model generation calls go to external services (HypiHub or your own keys) and cost money
cloning existing videos can infringe copyright: only recreate your own material
needs Node 22.15+ and pnpm

openui.name: OpenUI (W&B)
openui.provides: Standalone web app: describe a UI, see it rendered live, convert HTML to React/Svelte/Web Components. Needs your own LLM provider keys. Not a skill.
risks: not agent-integrable as a skill
prompt-to-UI output tends toward the generic look the designer pass removes
sends prompts to whichever LLM provider you configure

ponytail.name: Ponytail
ponytail.provides: One prompt that pushes agents to write less code (lite/full/ultra levels), plus /ponytail-review, /ponytail-audit, /ponytail-debt and a status band. Its benchmark figures are the project's own and unverified.
risks: registers hooks and a UI band; optional import reads your past Claude Code session data (kept local per README)
'less code' must never mean less testing, validation, error/empty states or accessibility: HyperSkill gates win
overlaps karpathy-skills (simplicity first): use one

slopmonster.name: SlopMonster
install: clone and copy the folder to ~/.claude/skills/slopmonster/
slopmonster.provides: tools/deslop.py: local checker that flags common AI-writing patterns in README/landing/email/script text and scores it out of 5; an optional second-model rewrite step.
risks: use only the local checker by default: tools/cleanse.sh sends your text to another AI CLI/provider (opt in per use)
a score is a hint, not proof of quality or originality

rea.name: REA (reverse engineering for agents)
install: npx rea-agents setup  (read it first; needs Node 22+)
rea.provides: Lets an agent analyse shipped artifacts (JavaScript and Electron bundles, .NET, APKs, native binaries, firmware, captures) through an MCP server, a skill and a CLI. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native engine.
risks: not bundled: a large toolkit with its own MCP server
use it only on software you own or are authorised to examine; its own disclaimer says so, and it grants no licence to Hopper, IDA or Ghidra
runtime capture runs the target with your user permissions
for this pipeline the fit is narrow: checking your own shipped bundle for leaked secrets, source maps and unexpected endpoints

api-anything.name: API Anything
api-anything.provides: Records a website's own requests and replays them as callable 'operations' over HTTP/MCP. Not on npm yet.
risks: can import cookies from local browser profiles and stores credentials under ~/.api-anything
automating sites you do not own can breach their terms of service
not needed by any phase: prefer official APIs

hyperfigure.name: Hyperfigure (bundled, skills/hyperfigure)
install: already bundled in this plugin at skills/hyperfigure; standalone: copy the folder into a skills folder
hyperfigure.provides: Crafted, interactive isometric figures that explain a technical idea as a working object: many small precise parts in SVG, WebGL shader layers and an optional 3D mode, nine worked examples, a drawing kit, audits, printable sheets. Derived from Anatomy by Ryan (MIT).
hyperfigure.vetted: 2026-10-21: derived from Anatomy (wheresryan22/anatomy, commit 1482e84, MIT) by renaming and removing its gallery-publishing flow; the rest is unchanged (see skills/hyperfigure/NOTICE.md). The original's scripts were skimmed for network use (only 127.0.0.1 for Chrome's debug port), process spawning (Chrome and node) and deletes (its own temporary profiles); not a line-by-line audit. Its own regression suite passes on this version.
risks: its checks start headless Chrome from local scripts and talk to it over localhost
needs Node 20.10 or later, plus Chrome or Chromium for the checks
adds about 27 MB to the plugin (mostly built example pages)
the 3D mode is marked beta by the original author
builds are long: its own guidance quotes hours for larger figures, so agree the size with the owner first

sitewright.name: Sitewright (the owner's own skill, bundled in packs/sitewright)
install: hyperskill.py integrations enable sitewright   (bundled pack, no download)
or standalone: git clone https://github.com/raj742133/sitewright && cd sitewright && ./install.sh
sitewright.provides: Generates a complete Next.js 15 site from picked modules (landing, sign-in, MFA accounts, publishing, dashboard, connect-a-phone, ingest API) from one site.json, with motion, icons and ready-made components, then drives it in headless Chromium at 1280, 390 and 360 px. Written by the project owner; read at README and site level, its scripts were not audited line by line.
risks: it generates a whole app and backend: choose it in the plan phase, before the stack is decided, or it will fight your own architecture
generated code is a starting point: the foundation, product, ship and harden gates still apply (auth, tenant scoping, validation, rate limits)
its templates fetch fonts from Google Fonts and icons from api.iconify.design, and the browser checks need Chromium: review that against your privacy and CSP decisions
sign-in and MFA modules ship development-only passwords and secrets in .env.local: replace them before any deploy
bundles Hairline (MIT, Lucas Marques) figures: keep packs/sitewright/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md with it

hallmark.name: Hallmark
install: or upstream: npx skills add nutlope/hallmark
hallmark.provides: Anti-AI-slop design skill: a hard floor of 16 rules, 48 themes dealt so builds do not converge, and scripts/sloplint.mjs, a zero-dependency linter that checks built HTML/CSS/JSX against those rules (FAIL, REFLEX and WARN grades, optional --render pass in a real browser).
risks: a second design voice: use it instead of taste-skill, not alongside it
do not run its install.mjs or install-hook.mjs: they edit .claude/settings.json, and HyperSkill already has its own hooks
scripts/imagegen.mjs sends prompts to Together AI, and only when TOGETHER_API_KEY is set
theme.mjs photos downloads Wikimedia Commons images only when asked; each keeps its own licence
sloplint writes a .hallmark/ folder into the project; --render needs puppeteer-core and Chrome
its stamp line must be the first line of the CSS; a lint pass shows the rules were followed, not that the design is good

humanizer.name: Humanizer
humanizer.provides: Rewrites AI-sounding prose so it reads like the writer, from Wikipedia's 'Signs of AI writing': staged openers, forced triads, inflated claims, stock words, formatting by rule. Keeps what the text says.
risks: it rewrites: review the diff, and keep every claim true (a smoother sentence is not a verified one)
overlaps SlopMonster: use one pass, not both

diagram-design.name: Diagram Design
diagram-design.provides: 45 diagram types (architecture, flowchart, sequence, state machine, ER, deployment, data flow, timeline, quadrant, swimlane and more) as one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG; can redraw Mermaid, draw.io and Excalidraw files; exports SVG and PNG.
risks: asks to customise the style guide on first use: answer it once, or keep the default
PNG export needs Playwright, which it does not install for you
a diagram is a claim: check each box and arrow against the code before the architecture-explained check

last30days.name: last30days (community research)
last30days.provides: Searches Reddit, Hacker News, YouTube, GitHub, Polymarket and more for what people said about a topic in the last 30 days, ranks by engagement and writes a cited brief. Several sources need no key.
risks: not bundled: the skill folder is about 18 MB
with a reasoning-provider key set, your topic and the retrieved snippets go to that provider
some sources use browser cookies or third-party scraping services (ScrapeCreators, Bright Data): check their terms and never give it a logged-in session you care about
engagement is not demand: treat the brief as evidence to weigh, never as proof of a market

scrapling.name: Scrapling (web extraction)
install: MCP server and agent skill: pip install "scrapling[ai]"
scrapling.provides: Python scraping framework: HTTP and browser fetchers, adaptive parsing that survives page changes, concurrent spiders, an MCP server and an official agent skill.
risks: not bundled: a Python library with browser downloads
its README says it is for educational and research use and that you must follow site terms, robots.txt and privacy law
its stealth fetchers are built to get past bot protection: do not use that on a site whose terms forbid scraping
scraped personal data is personal data: GDPR and similar apply

ui-library-choice.fallback: ask the owner; recommend with trade-offs

browser-verify.fallback: Playwright from the project's own e2e setup

canary.fallback: hs-operate monitoring plan and post-deploy checks

video.fallback: storyboard only; ask the owner to install HyperFrames

video-analysis.fallback: ffprobe + extracted frames inspected by hand

skill-installer.fallback: copy the SKILL.md directory manually after reading it

icons.fallback: the project's existing icon library; one collection only

design-reference.fallback: the owner's 2-3 reference products and screenshots

implementation-discipline.fallback: non-negotiable rules + test-first bug fixing in hs-ship

task-agents.fallback: sequential work on branches, or Claude subagents

voiceover.fallback: no voiceover; captions only, or the owner's own recording

copy-review.fallback: re-read the copy for filler, vague claims and AI tells; keep every claim traceable to a real feature

explainer-figure.fallback: a plain Mermaid or hand-written SVG diagram, with no interaction (see the diagramming guidance for artifacts)

site-scaffold.fallback: hand-written pages and routes following the hs-product design-system and the plan's architecture

architecture-diagram.fallback: draw the architecture and data flow as Mermaid in docs/system-design.md, then check every box and arrow against the code

design-lint.fallback: walk skills/hs-product/references/design-system.md and the design-critique slot's checklist by hand and record what you found

community-research.fallback: search the forums, issue trackers and review sites by hand with WebSearch; cite each thread and say what you could not find

web-extraction.fallback: read public pages with WebFetch, respect robots.txt and the site's terms, and never work around bot protection

artifact-analysis.fallback: inspect your own build output by hand: grep the bundle for secrets and internal URLs, and check that source maps are not published
